claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar-colony microstructure.
The two phases in the starting lamellar colonies are FCC and B2.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
A single cryogenic-rolling step without subsequent annealing will refine the dual-phase lamellar microstructure.
Cryogenic rolling should be performed at temperatures near that of liquid nitrogen.
The proposed process includes no annealing or other heat treatment before room-temperature tensile testing.
Cryogenic rolling alone will decrease lamellar-colony size.
Cryogenic rolling alone will produce ultrafine grain distributions in the FCC regions.
The refined microstructure will promote more homogeneous dislocation flow and reduce sharp internal boundaries.
Cryogenic deformation increases dislocation density and suppresses significant recovery.
Cryogenic processing promotes strain partitioning among the constituent phases.
Microstructural refinement will reduce dislocation pile-ups at phase boundaries.
Reduced dislocation pile-ups will alleviate local stress concentrations that initiate microcracking.
Cryogenic rolling without annealing will increase tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
The elongation to failure after cryogenic rolling alone may exceed approximately 14%.
Cryogenic rolling without annealing will maintain or slightly increase both yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Insufficient cooling may prevent formation of the microstructure needed to mitigate dislocation pile-ups.
Additional heat treatment may fail to produce the microstructure needed to mitigate dislocation pile-ups.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis excludes annealing and suggests that additional heat treatment may prevent the desired microstructure, whereas the cited same-system evidence obtained its hierarchical microstructure and simultaneous strength–ductility enhancement specifically through cryo-rolling followed by annealing.
